items.title: 64th Regular Session of the Sangguniang Bayan of Santa Cruz
items.excerpt: The Sangguniang Bayan of Santa Cruz convened its 64th Regular Session to deliberate on updated disaster preparedness and contingency plans for flood, storm surge, and landslide, alongside the CY 2027 Annual Investment Program of Barangay Bato.
items.content:
Continuing its commitment to responsive, proactive, and people-centered governance, the Sangguniang Bayan of Santa Cruz, Davao del Sur, convened its 64th Regular Session to deliberate on matters concerning disaster preparedness, public safety, and grassroots development.

Among the key agenda items taken up were the following:

  • MDRRMC Resolution No. 05, s. 2026 – Approving the LDRRMO Updated Contingency Plan on Flood with Emerging and Re-Emerging Infectious Disease Control Measures;
  • MDRRMC Resolution No. 06, s. 2026 – Approving the LDRRMO Updated Contingency Plan on Storm Surge with Emerging and Re-Emerging Infectious Disease Control Measures;
  • MDRRMC Resolution No. 07, s. 2026 – Approving the LDRRMO Updated Contingency Plan on Landslide with Emerging and Re-Emerging Infectious Disease Control Measures; and
  • CY 2027 Annual Investment Program (AIP) of Barangay Bato.

These agenda items highlight the importance of strengthening the municipality's disaster risk reduction and management capabilities while ensuring that development priorities at the barangay level receive due attention.

Good governance is not only about responding to today's needs, but also about preparing for tomorrow's challenges.

items.title: 63rd Regular Session of the Sangguniang Bayan of Santa Cruz
items.excerpt: The 63rd Regular Session tackled key legislative matters on public health, barangay development, supplemental budgets, disaster preparedness, and local transportation services in Santa Cruz, Davao del Sur.
items.content:
The Sangguniang Bayan of Santa Cruz, Davao del Sur, convened for its 63rd Regular Session, addressing legislative matters that advance public health, strengthen local governance, support barangay development, and promote the safety and welfare of Santa Cruzians.

Among the key agenda items referred for appropriate action were the request for the deployment of two physicians under the Department of Health’s Doctor to the Barrios (DTTB) Program, the review of various Barangay Annual Investment Programs (BAIPs) for CY 2027, and supplemental budgets intended to support local development priorities.

The session also included the proposed adoption of the municipality’s Supplemental Annual Investment Program (SAIP) No. 3 for CY 2026 amounting to ₱32.326 million, as well as the proposed designation of a municipal evacuation center site to strengthen disaster preparedness and emergency response.

Meanwhile, committee reports covered the proposed establishment of a Community-led Innovation Center (CLIC) in partnership with the Department of Science and Technology (DOST), the Tribal Council of Barangay Tibolo, and Davao del Sur State College (DSSC); the proposed grant of usufruct over an LGU-owned property for Barangay Zone II; and the review of Barangay Darong’s supplemental budget.

The agenda further included the review of barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan budgets, along with the recommendation concerning the issuance of authority to operate motorized tricycles-for-hire for 19 applicants and their corresponding routes.

items.title: 62ND REGULAR SESSION | SANGGUNIANG BAYAN OF SANTA CRUZ
items.excerpt: The Sangguniang Bayan of Santa Cruz tackled key legislative matters, including the Children’s Welfare Code, ₱210-million Supplemental Budget No. 4 for CY 2026, and priority development initiatives.
items.content:
The Sangguniang Bayan of Santa Cruz convened for its 62nd Regular Session, taking up legislative matters and development initiatives that reflect the municipality’s continuing commitment to good governance, social welfare, and sustainable development.

During the session, several matters were referred for appropriate legislative action, including the proposed implementation of the Gulayan sa Bayan Project in partnership with the Department of Agriculture and local organizations, the review of barangay supplemental budgets, the proposed ₱822.41-million Local Expenditures Program for FY 2027, and agreements supporting the implementation of the Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program (4Ps).

The Sanggunian also acted on significant measures under Third and Final Reading, including:

📌 Children’s Welfare Code of the Municipality of Santa Cruz — establishing comprehensive policies, programs, and mechanisms to protect children’s rights and promote their development, participation, and overall welfare.

📌 ₱210-Million Supplemental Budget No. 4, CY 2026 — providing funding for priority development projects, particularly the acquisition and development of the Government Center Annex and Santa Cruz Commercial and Tourism Hub, as well as the rehabilitation and improvement of the municipal water system.

items.excerpt: The Santa Cruz Franchising and Regulatory Board (SCFRB), presided over by Vice Mayor Atty. Charlotte Gallego, deliberates on franchise unit additions, dropping of units, and other transport concerns to promote a safer and more organized public transportation system.
items.content:

The Santa Cruz Franchising and Regulatory Board (SCFRB), presided over by Vice Mayor Atty. Charlotte Gallego, convened to deliberate on applications for the addition and dropping of franchise units, along with other transportation-related concerns.

items.title: 61st Regular Session of the Sangguniang Bayan
items.excerpt: The 61st Regular Session tackled key initiatives on education, the ₱210 million Supplemental Budget No. 4, municipal water system improvement, and child protection.
items.content:
Another session dedicated to advancing legislation, strengthening public services, and building a better future for every Santa Cruzan. ⚖️🏛️

The Sangguniang Bayan of Santa Cruz convened for its 61st Regular Session, taking up matters concerning education, local development, water system, and child protection.

Among the significant matters discussed were:

🏫 Establishment of a Stand-Alone Senior High School
The Sangguniang Bayan took up the follow-up request of Sta. Cruz National High School – Senior High School for legislative support in establishing a stand-alone senior high school in the municipality, an initiative aimed at expanding educational opportunities for our learners.

💰 Proposed ₱210 Million Supplemental Budget No. 4, CY 2026. The proposed supplemental budget was referred for appropriate legislative action to finance priority development projects, particularly the acquisition and development of the Sta. Cruz Commercial and Tourism Hub and the rehabilitation and improvement of the municipal water system.

👧🧒 Children’s Welfare Code of Santa Cruz- The proposed ordinance seeks to establish comprehensive programs, policies, mechanisms, and services for the protection, development, participation, and welfare of children, reaffirming the importance of safeguarding the rights and future of every child in our municipality.

items.title: 60TH REGULAR SESSION | SANGGUNIANG BAYAN OF SANTA CRUZ
items.excerpt: The Sangguniang Bayan convened its 60th Regular Session, advancing measures on barangay development, environmental governance, local economic development, and investment promotion.
items.content:
Another productive day of legislation and local governance as the Sangguniang Bayan convened its 60th Regular Session, deliberating on measures aimed at strengthening barangay development, environmental governance, and local economic growth.

Passed on Second Reading:
• Supplemental Barangay Annual Investment Program (SBAIP) No. 01, CY 2026 of Barangay Darong — ₱9,900,000.00
• SBAIP No. 02, CY 2026 of Barangay Zone II — ₱500,000.00
• SBAIP No. 02, CY 2026 of Barangay Jose Rizal — ₱478,145.29

Passed on Third and Final Reading:
• Municipal Ordinance No. 08 — Enacting the Local Economic Development and Investment Promotions (LEDIP) Code of the Municipality of Santa Cruz.
• Municipal Ordinance No. 09 — Creating the Municipal Environment and Natural Resources Office (MENRO) as a regular department, defining its functions and powers, creating plantilla positions, and providing the necessary appropriations.
• Municipal Ordinance No. 10 — Enacting the Revised Local Investment Incentive Code of the Municipality of Santa Cruz.

From barangay investments to environmental protection and investment promotion, every legislative measure is part of building a municipality that is organized, sustainable, investment-ready, and responsive to the needs of its people.🏛️👩‍⚖️📈

items.title: 59th Regular Session | Sangguniang Bayan of Santa Cruz
items.excerpt: 59th Regular Session tackling key legislative measures for local governance, development, and community needs.
items.content:
The Sangguniang Bayan of Santa Cruz, Davao del Sur conducted its 59th Regular Session, taking up a number of legislative matters aimed at strengthening local governance, advancing development initiatives, and responding to the needs of our community.

Among the matters tackled were:

📌 First Reading
• Proposed authority to enter into and sign a Deed of Mutual Cancellation of the Addendum to the MOA and Release of Remaining Funds with the Department of Transportation (DOTr) relative to the Mindanao Railway Project: Tagum–Davao–Digos Segment;
• Proposed MOA with Mercury Drug Corporation for the provision of medicines and medical supplies to qualified beneficiaries;
• Proposed Deed of Usufruct with Barangay Zone II for the use of LGU-owned property as a barangay site;
• Request for legislative support for the establishment of a Stand-Alone Senior High School in Santa Cruz;
• Proposed ₱210 Million Supplemental Budget No. 4, CY 2026, primarily for priority development projects, including the acquisition and development of the Santa Cruz Commercial and Tourism Hub and the rehabilitation/improvement of the municipal water system.

📌 Second Reading
• Draft Ordinance creating the Municipal Environment and Natural Resources Office (MENRO) as a regular department, including the creation of plantilla positions and corresponding appropriations;
• Draft Revised Local Investment Incentive Code of the Municipality of Santa Cruz.

📌 Unassigned Business
• SCFRB Resolution No. 011, s. 2026, recommending approval of the authority to operate Motorized Tricycle-for-Hire for 18 applicants and their corresponding routes of operation.

items.title: SCFRB Meeting: Advancing Orderly Transportation and Regulatory Measures
items.excerpt: The SCFRB discussed franchise applications, transportation law enforcement, a possible franchise moratorium, and the proposed Sibulan route to promote accessible, compliant, and orderly transportation in Santa Cruz.
items.content:
The Santa Cruz Franchising and Regulatory Board convened a meeting presided over by Vice Mayor Atty. Charlotte F. Gallego, together with Transpo Committee Chair Hon. Julius Rizada, tackling key transportation and regulatory concerns affecting commuters, drivers, and operators in the municipality.

Among the matters discussed were the applications for franchise of several individuals, the massive enforcement of transportation laws and regulations, the possible moratorium on the granting of new franchise applications, and the proposed opening of a transportation route in Barangay Sibulan.

The discussions underscored the need to balance public convenience, transportation accessibility, regulatory compliance, and the welfare of existing operators. 🏛️👩‍⚖️🚧
